question: The Commission has granted many energy projects the status of ‘projects of common interest’ (PCIs) or ‘projects of mutual interest’ (PMIs). These projects can enjoy a wide range of advantages. According to the Commission’s note of 1 December 2025, the projects will benefit from accelerated permitting and regulatory processes, among other things.

The objectives of boosting the EU’s competitiveness, phasing out fossil fuels and improving European self-sufficiency and energy security are of course worthy of support. We need more and more renewable energy. Accelerated procedures for the approval of projects could, however, raise concerns among local communities that are adversely affected by projects carried out in their area.

Subsidiarity is a key EU principle. In today’s world, energy projects should enjoy strong social acceptance in the areas they affect. For example, plans for hydropower projects in Northern Finland have sparked heated public debate locally.

With the above in mind: Do accelerated permitting and regulatory processes include sufficient elements to ensure that people in the areas affected by projects are adequately consulted and given opportunities to influence them, and that projects are socially acceptable?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.3.2026) Projects of Common and Mutual Interest (PCIs/PMIs) are infrastructure projects selected following the procedure in the Trans-European Networks for Energy (TEN-E) Regulation1, and benefit from the permit granting framework of its chapter III.

The Regulation contains measures dedicated to transparency and public participation2 where it establishes three main requirements as the minimum standard for PCIs/PMIs: a concept for public participation must be produced by promoters and approved by national competent authorities; at least one public consultation must take place at an early stage3; promoters must publish a report on the results of the consultation and how the opinions of the public were accounted in identifying the location, trajectory and design of the project4.

Furthermore, under the Pact for Engagement5, the Commission works with transmission and distribution system operators, regulators, and civil society to strengthen early, regular and meaningful public engagement in grid development projects. The Pact supports practical tools and guidance6 to improve transparency, feedback on how input is used, and build social acceptance alongside accelerated permitting.

The European Grids Package proposal7, includes a revised TEN-E Regulation8 and a Directive to accelerate permit-granting9. These acts restate requirements for early and meaningful public consultations and introduce new requirements for renewable energy projects in terms of benefits sharing and deploying an independent facilitator for dialogues with the public.
Therefore, the Commission expects that people in the areas affected are adequately consulted and can influence the project, fostering public acceptance and support for these key energy projects.
1 Regulation (EU) 2022/869 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May 2022 on guidelines for

trans-European energy infrastructure, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/869/oj/eng. 2 Article 9 of the TEN-E Regulation. 3 This should always be before the permit granting application is submitted and support the identification of the most suitable location, trajectory and technology. 4 In the case they were not taken into account promoters need to justify why the public views were not taken into account.

5 Launched in 2023 under the EU Action Plan for Grids, https://energy.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-launchesnew-pact-engagement-electricity-sector-2023-11-28_en. 6 E.g. work on public engagement plans. 7 ‘Commission proposes upgrade of the EU's energy infrastructure to lower bills and boost independence’, Press Release, 10 December 2025: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_25_2945.

8 Proposal for revised Trans-European Network for Energy (TEN-E) Regulation COM(2025) 1006 final https://energy.ec.europa.eu/publications/proposal-revised-trans-european-network-energy-ten-e-regulationcom2025-1006-final_en. 9 Proposal for revised Directive to accelerate permit-granting procedures of infrastructure projects COM(2025) 1007 final https://energy.ec.europa.
